message.content:
Answer: C
Reason: The clinical presentation of tracheal stenosis causing recurrent respiratory infections in an older adult, combined with the explicit absence of ear, nose, and joint symptoms (which rules out relapsing polychondritis), is most characteristic of tracheobronchial amyloidosis. This condition typically presents as diffuse or nodular submucosal infiltration leading to airway narrowing without the systemic cartilaginous inflammation seen in polychondritis.
